primary_task: Write a review-governance.cedar policy that gates AI agent review actions (gh pr review/merge, CI file edits, protected-branch pushes) behind human approval.

requirements.name: plugin-default-policy-file
requirements.evidence: 1. **Start with the plugin's default.** Copy `./plugins/review-agent-governance/policies/review-agent-governance.cedar` to `./review-governance.cedar` and edit from there.
requirements.basis: "read": "read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)" - the manifest does not say whether this plugin is present in the working directory.

requirements.name: write
requirements.evidence: Copy ... to `./review-governance.cedar` and edit from there.

requirements.name: protect-mcp
requirements.basis: "bash": "... install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, ...)"

notes: Unknown: whether ./plugins/review-agent-governance/policies/review-agent-governance.cedar exists in the working directory (check with glob). If it is missing, the policy can still be written from scratch, so it is not counted as blocking (unknown does not block per rubric); if the plugin could be fetched it would come from GitHub, which is allow-listed. protect-mcp is needed only to evaluate/enforce the policy, not to write it. The gh/glab commands named are the subjects of the policy, not tools the agent runs.
